reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: original § 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of bespoke Deliverables (which expressly exclude Vendor Technology and know-how under § 1.4) in Vendor and leaves Customer only a revocable, term-limited licence — directly contrary to the preferred position that Customer owns what it pays for.

The redline is directionally correct and minimal: it flips ownership to Customer with an express irrevocable assignment and redirects the existing limited licence to Vendor, without disturbing acceptable neighbouring provisions (14.1 Customer Data/IP, 14.3 Vendor Technology with the § 13.2 perpetual licence-back, 14.4 no joint ownership).

Rule coverage is complete in context: a separate Customer Data ownership clause already exists (14.1), Vendor's embedded-IP licence-back is preserved via 14.3/13.2, and no joint ownership language remains; deterministic checks confirm no residual assignment of Customer Data/IP to Vendor.

Comment complies with tone and format requirements — first person plural, prefixed, explains the change and the playbook basis, and offers the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, sublicensable licence fallback if Vendor cannot assign.
The residual revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence now running to Vendor does not prejudice Customer and is the least-invasive way to reverse the clause's direction.
